title: QUIC RFC 9000 Client 0-RTT Updated Transport-Parameter Packet-Use Policy
purpose: Describe the bounded internal policy that keeps 0-RTT packet construction on remembered transport-parameter values and treats updated-value use as a protocol violation candidate.
design_summary: QuicZeroRttTransportParameterPolicy now has an internal packet-use decision seam that combines the packet protection level with the source of a transport-parameter value. 0-RTT packets are allowed to use remembered transport-parameter values only. Updated values learned from the server handshake or from 1-RTT frames are rejected for 0-RTT use with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION semantics, while updated values are accepted only once the sender is constructing 1-RTT packets. A server-side helper maps detected updated-value use in 0-RTT to the optional PROTOCOL_VIOLATION connection-error policy.
data_and_state_considerations: The policy is intentionally source-classification based. It does not admit early data, decrypt 0-RTT, parse frames to infer value provenance, or persist new public state; future sender and receiver integration can feed the same source classification into the policy without widening public early-data support.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Unknown value provenance fails closed for client 0-RTT packet use without asserting a server protocol violation.
Updated handshake and 1-RTT-frame values are rejected outside 1-RTT packet construction.
Remembered values remain the only accepted source for 0-RTT packets.
The server helper assumes the caller has already classified the offending value source.
risks: Future real 0-RTT sender integration must preserve the same source classification rather than treating updated connection limits as immediately usable by 0-RTT packets.
Future real 0-RTT receiver integration must classify offending frame behavior before invoking the optional PROTOCOL_VIOLATION policy.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes only the S7P4P1 updated-value packet-use tail. It does not claim public early-data APIs, TLS early_data extension admission wiring, anti-replay behavior, 0-RTT decryption, application-data delivery, or hosted interop readiness.
